models_evaluated: customised GPT with static domain knowledge (GPTs, o3)

links.outcome: Agreement with expert benchmark for systemic therapy: grounded (RAG, static corpus) vs baseline GPT
links.effect: RAG and GPTs 70.0% agreement vs baseline GPT 60.0%; RAG and GPTs met the -10% non-inferiority margin, baseline did not; neither met -5%.
links.quote: Based on the lower bound of the one-sided 95% bootstrap confidence interval, GPT did not meet non-inferiority, whereas GPTs and RAG satisfied the –10% but not the –5% margin (Fig. 1 ).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of outputs across repeated runs of the same cases
links.effect: RAG perfect stability (AC1 1.000); baseline GPT AC1 0.843; GPTs lower (about 0.766, 69.9% agreement); temperature 0.2 used.
links.quote: Baseline GPT was more reproducible than GPTs (AC1 0.843, 95% CI 0.687–0.961; 80.1%, 95% CI 60–95 vs 69.9%, 95% CI 50–90), yielding the ranking RAG > GPT > GPTs.

links.outcome: Explicit expression of uncertainty in AI vs expert recommendations
links.effect: AI expressed uncertainty more consistently than experts: GPTs AC1 1.000, RAG 0.875, GPT 0.835 vs experts 0.239 (p<0.001).
links.quote: Uncertainty was more frequently acknowledged by AI than experts.

links.outcome: Concordance of AI therapy recommendations with expert modal guideline-based decisions
links.effect: Agreement 60.0% (GPT), 70.0% (GPTs, RAG) vs experts 63.8%; lung primaries significantly predicted disagreement for RAG (OR 19.50, p=0.032); AI outputs always complete.
links.quote: These findings indicate that adapted LLMs can deliver guideline-concordant therapeutic recommendations close to expert consensus, although validation in prospective, real-world studies remains essential before clinical use.

models_evaluated: customised GPT with static domain knowledge (GPTs)

links.outcome: Agreement with expert systemic therapy benchmark
links.effect: GPT 60.0%; GPTs 70.0%; RAG 70.0%; GPTs/RAG met –10% but not –5% non-inferiority.
links.quote: Against this benchmark, baseline GPT achieved 60.0% (95% CI 44.4–76.9), GPTs 70.0% (95% CI 54.5–85.7), and the retrieval-augmented model (RAG) 70.0% (95% CI 54.5–84.6).

links.effect: GPTs and RAG satisfied –10% but not –5% margin; baseline GPT did not meet non-inferiority.
links.quote: Based on the lower bound of the one-sided 95% bootstrap confidence interval, GPT did not meet non-inferiority, whereas GPTs and RAG satisfied the –10% but not the –5% margin (Fig. 1 ).

links.effect: RAG/GPTs agreement 70.0%; baseline GPT 60.0%; concordance remained limited and baseline was not non-inferior.
links.quote: Baseline GPT reached 60.0% and was not non-inferior.

links.effect: RAG AC1 1.000; GPT AC1 0.843; GPTs AC1 0.766 for therapeutic recommendations.
links.quote: ARTEMIS therefore provides the first evidence that repeated generations from the same model yield highly consistent therapeutic recommendations, particularly for the RAG configuration (AC1 1.000) and, to a slightly lesser extent, for GPT and GPTs (AC1 0.843 and 0.766, respectively).
